## Recode for acq



1. Create a dictionary with semantic pairs,  unbalanced positive and negative items per scale 
2. Calculate acq indexes general and specific 
3. Calculate within pole inconsistencies 
4. Correct item responses for acq

```{r}
# arguments

item_dic <- senna_dic
df <- data_senna

# acq_index general

coditem_acq <- senna_dic %>% 
 dplyr::mutate(item_pair = as.integer(!is.na(seman_pairs))) %>%
 dplyr::filter(item_pair ==1) %>%
 dplyr::pull(coditem) %>%
 unique


 # Acquiescence index and sds global
 acq_index<- apply(df[, coditem_acq], MARGIN = 1, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
 acq_sd <-  apply(df[, coditem_acq], MARGIN = 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE) 
 acq_sd <- ifelse(acq_sd == 0, NA, acq_sd)
 
 acq_index_global <- tibble(
  acq_index  = index_acq,
  acq_sd = acq_sd
 )
 
# Acquiescence index per scale
acq_dic <- senna_dic %>% 
 dplyr::mutate(item_pair = as.integer(!is.na(seman_pairs))) %>%
 dplyr::filter(item_pair ==1) %>%
 dplyr::group_by(scale) %>%
 dplyr::summarise(items =  list(coditem)) %>%
 dplyr::ungroup()


scales <- acq_dic$scale
items <- acq_dic$items

# Initialize the list
acq_index_by_scale <- vector("list", length(scales))

for (i in seq_along(scales)) {
  acq_index_by_scale[[i]] <- apply(df[, items[[i]] ], MARGIN = 1, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(acq_index_by_scale)[i] <- paste0("acq_index_", scales[[i]])
}

# Convert to a data frame if needed
acq_index_by_scale_df <- as.data.frame(acq_index_by_scale)


# inconsistency unbalanced scales


unbalance_dic <- item_dic %>% 
 dplyr::mutate(item_pair = as.integer(!is.na(seman_pairs))) %>%
 dplyr::group_by(scale, item_pair, pole) %>%
 dplyr::summarise(items =  list(coditem)) %>%
 dplyr::ungroup() %>%
 tidyr::pivot_wider(
  names_from = c(item_pair, pole), 
  values_from = items) %>%
 purrr::set_names("scale", "unbl_neg", "unbl_pos", "bal_neg", "bal_pos") %>%
 dplyr::mutate(
  pos = !purrr::map_lgl(unbl_pos, is.null) & !purrr::map_lgl(bal_pos, is.null), 
  neg = !purrr::map_lgl(unbl_neg, is.null) & !purrr::map_lgl(bal_neg, is.null)
  ) %>%
 dplyr::filter((pos | neg))




is.null(unbalance_dic[["0_0"]])
```
